question: What is the meaning of global warming potential (gwp) in relation to material layers, materials?
description: Global warming potential (GWP) in relation to material layers and materials refers to the measure of how much heat a greenhouse gas traps in the atmosphere over a specific time period, usually 100 years, compared to carbon dioxide. It is used to assess the environmental impact of materials based on their ability to contribute to global warming.

3.  Development of a Level(s) conform CMP 
3.1.  Relevant indicators in the Level(s) framework 
The Level(s) framework consists of six macro-objectives that describe a building’s sustainability. The 
macro-objectives can be tracked through sixteen indicators. The macro-objectives describe different 
perspectives of sustainability: greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions and energy use, material requirements 
and waste production, water use, indoor quality, future resilience considering climate change, and 
economic costs. Even though these objectives are interlinked, the most important one, regarding a CMP, 
is macro-objective 2 “Resource efficient and circular material life cycles”, which is quantified through 
four indicators: 
i. 
Bill of quantities (BoQ), bill of materials (BoM) and lifespans 
ii. 
Construction and demolition waste (CDW) 
iii. 
Design for adaptability and renovation 
iv. 
Design for deconstruction (DfD) 
The following subsection describes existing barriers for CMP and looks at the Level(s) framework for 
possible mitigation measures. In this way, the proposed structure for a CMP in this paper integrates the 
relevant indicators from Level(s). 
3.2.  Current barriers and possible solutions for CMP 
Even though material passports have been identified as a valuable solution to promote circularity in 
buildings, it is a recent tool and not widely used in the sector. In this context, a state-of-the-art analysis 
is required to identify the main barriers associated with the development and use of material passports.  
An overview of the identified barriers and the considered mitigation measures adopted in the present 
paper are summarized in Table 1. They are explained in more detail in the following subsections.

3.2.1.  Lack of awareness and standardization.
